subject: HostEval follow-up: pilot readiness + deployment preference recap
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Turner <alec.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: HostEval — quick post-demo recap and checklist

Alec / Priya — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary:
- Goal: proof-of-value for our hosted API powering FinLytics’ summary + extraction flows (low-latency customer replies).
- Primary constraint: 99th-percentile latency target ~150ms on short prompts, peak bursts expected during business hours (~350 rps burst).
- Data residency: US-only for now; no on-prem requirement on day 0.

Proposed evaluation path (hosted first):
1) Sandbox sandbox endpoints (hosted) for integration and functional validation — 2-week quickstart cadence.
2) Traffic slice & ratebound: start with 50 rps sustained, up to 350 rps burst for 1 hour. We’ll instrument tracing and cost counters.
3) Ops readiness: canary endpoints + prefix/KV caching to shave token costs.

Deliverables I’ll send after this email: hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf (attachment), and a short Ops playbook for canary routing.

Next steps:
- You confirm the sandbox contact and preferred start week.
- We’ll provision a sandbox API key and a staging endpoint (no cost for the 2-week trial).
- Schedule a 30-min integration preflight with FinLytics infra next week.

If you have immediate blockers that push you to Dedicated or Private, flag below and we’ll capture requirements (SLA, sustained throughput, data plane controls).

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf (1 page — checklist of onboarding steps & required config)

From: Alec Turner <alec.turner@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HostEval — quick post-demo recap and checklist

Thanks, Ben — good summary. A couple quick clarifying questions from our infra/engineering side: 

1) Rate limits: when you say 50 rps sustained / 350 rps burst, what are the enforced rate limits on sandbox endpoints versus hosted production? Do you do per-API-key or per-account throttles?
2) Fallbacks: if we hit capacity on hosted during a burst, what automatic fallbacks exist? Can requests be routed to a lower-cost model variant or queued briefly?
3) Data handling & logs: we need to confirm log retention and whether we can disable retention for certain endpoints during the trial.

Also — current thinking on our side: if hosted can hit the latency + burst SLA with predictable cost controls, we’ll start there. If not, we’ll need to evaluate Dedicated (reserved GPUs) for predictable throughput. No on-prem requirement yet, but we may need Private in 6–12 months depending on compliance reviews.

Can your team capture typical token/unit costs for the configuration you think is closest to our workload?

—Alec
Alec Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, FinLytics
alec.turner@finlytics.com | +1 (206) 555-8890

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Turner <alec.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finlytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 May 2025 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HostEval — quick post-demo recap and checklist

Alec — great questions. Short answers up front, then specifics below.

Short answers:
- Sandbox vs prod rate limits: sandbox endpoints are per-account keys with soft caps (we set the slice per trial). Production hosted uses per-account rate limits with the option to pre-approve higher envelopes for paid usage.
- Fallbacks: yes — our routing supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants and region-level capacity tiers. We can also configure immediate 503->retry behavior or graceful degradation to a cheaper quantized variant.
- Logs: you can opt out of long-term retention on trial endpoints; audit logs and KMS controls are only enabled in Private/Dedicated if you require customer-managed keys.

Details / recommended config for your profile:
- Recommend hosted quickstart: start with m-family open model (quantized) for latency — typically meets ~120–160ms 99p on short prompts on our hosted fleet. Enable prefix KV caching for repeated context (saves ~30% token cost).
- Rate setup for trial: we’ll provision sandbox with slice = 50 rps sustained, burst bucket = 350 rps for up to 60 minutes/day. These are adjustable mid-trial; we monitor and raise alerts if CPU/GPU saturation approaches thresholds.
- Cost example: approximate unit cost for the suggested config: $0.0035 / 1k tokens served (quantized m-family) — I’ll send a short pricing note in a separate doc but we can do a trial uplift credit if you want to ramp with higher bursts.

Ops/next steps I’ll action this morning:
- Provision sandbox endpoints and API keys (Monica will handle).
- Share a short playbook for canary routing, and a list of endpoints we’ll create (staging, preflight, canary).
- Schedule a 30-min preflight with FinLytics infra — propose Thu 05/29 10:00 AM PT; please confirm.

If after the trial the 99p latency or cost profile doesn’t match your needs, we can scope Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) — typical trigger conditions: sustained >300 rps with strict latency SLA or strict KMS/HSM/customer-managed key requirement. Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option if SOC/compliance requires fully customer-managed plane.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Turner <alec.turner@finlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 May 2025 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HostEval — quick post-demo recap and checklist

Alec — Monica on the Ops side here. I’ve provisioned the sandbox slice and attached a lightweight ops playbook to help your infra team run the integration preflight. Key notes for your engineers: 

- Endpoints we created:
  - staging.finlytics.redwood-hosted (staging, no retention by default)
  - canary.finlytics.redwood-hosted (canary, prefix KV cache enabled)

- Rate knobs implemented: per-account slice = 50 rps sustained, burst bucket = 350 rps (60 min/day). We enforce at the account layer and return standard 429 when exceeded; we recommend client-side backoff + retry with jitter.
- Fallbacks: configured automatic routing to a quantized-compatible variant; we also enabled an emergency fallback code path to return a cached summary if the model route is unavailable.

I attached redwood_ops_playbook.md (contains curl examples, header expectations, and a short troubleshooting checklist).

Please confirm Thu 05/29 10:00 AM PT works for preflight and share the best engineer contact.

—Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_ops_playbook.md (markdown, 2 pages — endpoints, backoff recipes, sample queries)
